evidence.finding: The subgroup beginning ghṛ and continuing to the end of Juhotyadi is marked Vedic. The commentary explains i-reduplication as Vedic; ṛ is explicitly also allowed in classical use.
Ordinary ṛ reduplication changes to a under7.4.66; this accounts for the VP a-form but does not license the lexical input in classical scope.
Independent primary Dhatupatha edition lists ghṛ/hṛ/sṛ/bhas/ki/kit/tur/dhiṣ/dhan/jan/gā as Vedic.

prospective_quarantine.exception_reason: Primary commentary explicitly permits ṛ also in bhāṣā.
prospective_quarantine.scope: All lakaras, prayogas, derivation recipes and scores for these dictionary entries. Future cohorts only; originals immutable.

policy_status: Worker recommendation to coordinator; shared helper/policy not mutated.
limits: The exact source explicitly allows a classical exception for ṛ. No other exception is established here.
